quote: The two-tier model means that the central bank does not have direct customer contact, information about the identity of individual CBDC account holders or conducts CBDC transactions in the ledger.
modality: conditional: two-tier model; listed as a rough-draft design feature
justification: The latest report (doc 6 p. 16) states that the central bank holds no identity information on account holders. This is about structural capability, not merely non-use, so it satisfies the pseudonymisation rule: the CB holds no routine identity key. The test documents corroborate this with tested status: identity data stay at the banks (doc 7 p. 11; doc 7 p. 10; doc 6 p. 11). The status is only 'option' because doc 6 p. 16 calls all design features a 'rough draft' after the adopted decision not to issue now. Evidence is therefore partial, not documented. Earlier account-based alternatives with CB linkage (doc 2 p. 31; doc 4 p. 24) were options that were not carried forward.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p. 24: I en lukket kontoløsning vil enhver beholdning være knyttet til en identifiserbar person.

quote: Banks are responsible for customer onboarding and for linking customers to ledger addresses that are registered in the banks’ own account registers. Only addresses approved by banks can hold and use retail CBDC.
justification: Under §6.5, premise (i) is documented for the latest design version: banks hold the address→person mapping (doc 7 p. 9; doc 6 p. 12). Premises (ii) and (iii) are not documented for that version. No finding states that banks routinely see the transaction records. The 2021 statement that interface providers must receive counterparty information (doc 4 p. 23) is conditional and concerns a different design version, so it cannot complete the inference. Customer relationship plus KYC alone is insufficient, so the value is n/d.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p. 23: tilbydere av brukergrensnitt må ha en mulighet til å motta informasjon om hvem en bruker mottar DSP fra og hvem en bruker overfører DSP til.

quote: Fifth, it must be clarified who is to be responsible for transaction monitoring under the Anti-Money Laundering Act with respect to CBDCs.
justification: The most specific and latest statement leaves responsibility for AML transaction monitoring open (doc 6 p. 22; also doc 5 p. 14). 'Same as for other payment services' (doc 6 p. 16) names no holder, so the contract rule gives n/d. The 2021 option assigning STRs to third parties (doc 4 p. 23) is not carried into the later reports, which explicitly treat the question as unresolved. The court-order mention in doc 6 p. 12 is a risk description from testing, not a documented route.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p. 23: identitetskontroll ved on-boarding av brukere, kontroll med transaksjoner og rapportering av mistenkelige transaksjoner.

quote: Siden løsningen er kombinert med lokal lagring, kan anonyme forhåndsbetalte kort gi anonymitet innenfor rammene av tillatt omfang.
modality: conditional: closed account solution with local storage
justification: No document contains an adopted offline commitment. Offline appears only as a desirable or required property in working-group reports (doc 2 p. 11; doc 3 p. 4; doc 4 p. 21), and the 2026 draft features contain no offline finding. Where privacy is discussed, the options point in both directions: anonymous prepaid cards (doc 4 p. 24) versus disallowing anonymity offline (doc 4 p. 40). Synchronisation linkage is unstated (doc 4 p. 40). An option cannot set yes or no, and an offline mode without privacy description is unknown.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p. 40: dersom systemet åpner for anonyme betalinger, vil dette være utilgjengelig i offline-situasjoner.

quote: For både hovedløsningen og den alternative løsningen kan det vurderes om det bør være mulighet for begrenset tilgang for personer som ikke tilfredsstiller kravene som nevnt over, for eksempel for turister og andre som midlertidig oppholder seg i Norge.
limits: smaller amounts; possibly time-limited; one counterparty fully KYC'd
justification: Low-identification routes appear only as considered options. These are a limited tier for tourists (doc 2 p. 26) and anonymous prepaid cards (doc 4 p. 24); neither is adopted, and whether identity verification is absent is unclear. The §6.6a inference to 'no' is blocked because project documents do mention lower-identification routes. F8 is also only an option. The value is therefore n/d, neither yes nor no.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p. 24: anonyme forhåndsbetalte kort gi anonymitet innenfor rammene av tillatt omfang.

quote: KYC and AML checks of CBDC users would have to be performed by banks or other market participants that offer wallets for CBDC storage and transactions to their customers.
justification: Every design iteration requires KYC at wallet providers for standard users. Supporting findings: a bank account as prerequisite (doc 2 p. 26), third-party KYC at onboarding (doc 4 p. 41), banks keeping CDD duties (doc 5 p. 14), and bank onboarding in the sandbox (doc 7 p. 9). The latest statement is a rough-draft design feature (doc 6 p. 16), so the status is option and evidence partial rather than documented and adopted.

quote: If the ledger address of an end-user can be linked to an identity – either through banks, court orders, technical leaks or data collocation – any participant with read access to the ledger would be able to view the entire transaction history related to this address.
actor: banks / courts / any participant with ledger read access
modality: conditional: identity link via banks, court orders, leaks or data collocation
justification: The tested retail design permits retrospective attribution once an address is linked to an identity, with banks and court orders named as linking sources (doc 6 p. 12; doc 7 p. 11). Earlier options describe identity linkage for large or suspicious transactions (doc 4 p. 24). They also describe keys that authorised actors can unlock after certain procedures (doc 4 p. 38). None is an adopted, defined procedure, so the status is tested and evidence partial. This finding qualifies F1 = no rather than contradicting it.

quote: CBDC should not be programmable money, and programmability, if implemented, should be at the payment service level.
justification: The latest draft design features exclude programmable money. They also state that CBDC must be usable regardless of conditions (doc 6 p. 17). This is a rough-draft feature after the decision not to issue, hence option and partial. Earlier working-group findings that Norges Bank could impose restrictions (doc 4 p. 16) or that social support could be purpose-bound (doc 4 p. 41) were hypothetical options. Confiscation in the prototype (doc 5 p. 8) has no stated purpose.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p. 16: kan Norges Bank legge inn føringer/begrensninger for tjenestene tredjeparter kan utføre og transaksjoner brukerne kan gjennomføre.

quote: Norges Bank will therefore be ready to introduce a central bank digital currency if it becomes necessary to maintain an efficient and secure payment system.
justification: The decision quoted in doc 6 ties any future issuance to maintaining an efficient and secure payment system. Every report repeats this rationale (doc 1 p. 5; doc 3 p. 3; doc 4 p. 4; doc 5 p. 5; doc 5 p. 15 Strategy 25). It is the only objective not rejected in the 2026 conclusions.
counter_evidence: doc 1 p. 33: vurderer derfor ikke at det kostnadsmessige argumentet for å innføre DSP i Norge er av avgjørende betydning.

quote: Introducing a retail CBDC is not a suitable measure for financial inclusion in Norway.
justification: Doc 6 explicitly rejects inclusion as a rationale. This is consistent with the 2019 view that access problems argue for keeping cash (doc 2 p. 12). Accessibility statements (doc 1 p. 30; doc 4 p. 14) are design requirements, not declared objectives.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p. 14: Det er også deler av befolkningen som på ulike måter kan ha utfordringer med å benytte elektroniske betalingsmåter.

quote: Introducing a retail CBDC could become relevant if necessary national control over the payment system is at risk, but this is not currently the case.
modality: conditional: if national control over payment system at risk
justification: National control over the payment system is a recurring declared rationale (doc 2 p. 6; doc 4 p. 4; doc 5 p. 6; doc 6 p. 9). In 2026 it is kept as the condition under which issuance would become relevant. The monetary-policy transmission strand is rejected (doc 5 p. 13; doc 6 p. 20), and the currency-substitution risk is judged minor (doc 5 p. 7). The flag is therefore conditional, with option status and partial evidence.
counter_evidence: doc 5 p. 13: CBDC should not primarily be seen as a monetary policy instrument

quote: Payment solutions using retail CBDCs could enhance the payment system's contingency arrangements, but contingency considerations do not at present provide a decisive argument for the introduction of a retail CBDC.
justification: Contingency and declining cash use motivated the exploration from 2018 to 2023 (doc 1 p. 4; doc 2 p. 5; doc 4 p. 4; doc 5 p. 3). The 2026 conclusion, restated in doc 6 p. 6, holds that contingency is not a decisive argument now. Under the supersession rule the later conclusion on the same matter governs, so the flag is no rather than yes. The value depends on reading 'not decisive' as a withdrawal of the objective; this is a definitional judgement.
counter_evidence: doc 6 p. 5: particular emphasis on whether ... it would be a suitable instrument to strengthen contingency arrangements in Norway's payment system.

quote: DSPs primære funksjon er å fremme et sikkert og effektivt betalingssystem, og andre funksjoner kan komme i konflikt med dette formålet.
justification: No document declares AML/CFT or tax enforcement as an objective. Doc 4 cautions against using CBDC for other authorities' purposes. Tax-tracing wishes are attributed to other authorities, not to Norges Bank (doc 4 p. 43). Crime-detection remarks are trade-off discussion (doc 1 p. 18). The cautionary statement comes from a working-group report (option), hence partial.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p. 43: noen myndigheter vekt på at DSP utformes slik at det er enkelt å spore opp pengenes opprinnelse

quote: Introducing a retail CBDC is not an appropriate measure at this stage to promote innovation that enhances effective and secure payment services.
justification: Innovation and competition were repeatedly cited as possible benefits (doc 1 p. 33; doc 2 p. 17; doc 4 p. 25; doc 5 p. 7; doc 6 p. 17). The 2026 conclusion rejects retail CBDC as an innovation measure at this stage, and under supersession the later conclusion on the same matter governs. As with contingency, coding no depends on reading 'not at this stage' as a withdrawal of the objective.
counter_evidence: doc 6 p. 17: A presumed purpose of introducing CBDC was that it would boost innovation in the use of blockchain technology.

quote: If CBDC is introduced, the argument in favour of this should primarily be linked to the payment system and not be thought of as an additional monetary policy instrument.
justification: Doc 5 explicitly ranks the payment-system rationale as primary. This matches earlier statements of the primary function or main motivation (doc 4 p. 41; doc 4 p. 62; doc 1 p. 4). The 2026 adopted readiness statement ties issuance to the payment system alone (doc 6 p. 2). The ranking itself appears only in working-group text, so the status is option and evidence partial. Doc 6 p. 17 notes that the purpose still needs clarification.
counter_evidence: doc 6 p. 17: This limit should be set following further clarification of purpose and areas of application.

value: safe/secure and efficient payment system in NOK
quote: Norges Bank will therefore be ready to introduce a central bank digital currency if it becomes necessary to maintain an efficient and secure payment system.
justification: The adopted readiness decision and the working-group rankings (doc 5 p. 13; doc 4 p. 41) both point to an efficient and secure payment system as the primary objective. The decision is adopted, but the explicit ranking comes from option-status texts, so evidence is partial.
counter_evidence: doc 6 p. 9: So far, there are no sufficient arguments that Norges Bank should introduce either a retail or a wholesale CBDC in the near future.

quote: Should Norges Bank issue a CBDC solution on a ledger, the Bank must decide whether this ledger should be public or private.
justification: No ledger choice has been made. The 2023 report calls a conclusion premature (doc 5 p. 10), and the 2026 draft leaves the public/private choice open while saying only that the ledger 'should probably' be blockchain-based (doc 6 p. 17, a rough draft). Platforms appear only as tests: a private Ethereum network (doc 5 p. 8), OpenCBDC (doc 5 p. 8) and Hyperledger Besu (doc 6 p. 11; doc 7 p. 9). Tested platforms carry status 'tested', never adopted, so the value is undecided rather than permissioned_DLT. Platform (tested): Hyperledger Besu.
counter_evidence: doc 6 p. 17: The ledger for CBDC holdings and transactions should probably be based on blockchain technology.
